# SOP-P1-L3-01 Line startup - Machining line
Revision: Rev D
Plant: P1, line P1-L3
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, EQ-P1-L3-CN03
Related documents: ECN-2026-029, SB-1026, SOP-P1-L3-02

Purpose
1. Define the required sequence and verification steps for safe startup of the Machining line at P1-L3. This procedure applies to operators and maintenance personnel responsible for EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and EQ-P1-L3-CN03.

Preconditions (required before step 1)
2. Authorizing supervisor present and briefed on any outstanding work orders that affect the line. See ECN-2026-029 for configuration changes and SB-1026 for safety bulletins affecting startup behavior.
3. All required lockout/tagout completed for maintenance activities and cleared from the line.
4. Electrical distribution and air/gas supplies to line declared available by Facilities. Confirmed isolation points match drawings in SOP-P1-L3-02.
5. The lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is CFW-LUB-497. Verify correct stock and fill records before applying lubricant.

PPE
6. Required PPE for all personnel: safety eyewear, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, flame-resistant clothing, and steel-toe footwear. Supervisors must verify PPE compliance prior to entry on the shop floor.

Startup sequence and verification steps
7. Equipment visual check
   7.1. Walk the line to confirm no foreign objects, debris, or tools remain on or adjacent to EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, or EQ-P1-L3-CN03.
   7.2. Verify guarding is installed and interlocks show closed condition at control panels.
   Rationale: A thorough visual inspection reduces risk of immediate mechanical interference and protects interlock health.

8. Induction heater initial condition (EQ-P1-L3-IH01)
   8.1. Confirm coolant level and flow indicator are within operational range per manufacturer guidance.
   8.2. Verify electrical connections and control cabinet doors are secured.
   8.3. Confirm the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C and that the PLC setpoint matches that value prior to energizing the heater.
   Rationale: Correct setpoint prevents thermal nonconformance and downstream machining issues. Example: if PLC setpoint does not read 1235 °C, do not proceed; isolate and contact maintenance.

9. Hydraulic forging press pre-energize (EQ-P1-L3-HP02)
   9.1. Confirm hydraulic fluid level and filter condition; verify lubricant inventory includes CFW-LUB-497 and that the fill is logged.
   9.2. Confirm accumulator and reservoir covers installed and that there are no visible leaks.
   9.3. Energize hydraulic power using local control and verify control feedback indicates ready state before actuating any cylinder movement.
   Rationale: Using the specified lubricant prevents pump and valve damage and ensures hydraulic response meets design assumptions.

10. CNC machining cell checks (EQ-P1-L3-CN03)
   10.1. Verify tool magazine installed and that basic interlock tests pass at the operator HMI.
   10.2. Confirm part program selection matches job traveler information from production release in SOP-P1-L3-02.
   Rationale: Program mismatch is a common source of scrap and tool damage; verification avoids costly failures.

11. Dry run sequence
   11.1. Execute a dry run at reduced functional steps without material in the flow path to confirm motion sequences and interlock behavior.
   11.2. Observe emergency stops and verify stop response from all stations on the line.
   Rationale: Dry runs validate control logic and reveal mechanical interference before live billets are introduced.

12. First-billet introduction
   12.1. Introduce the first billet only after all preceding checks are complete and documented.
   12.2. Monitor temperature readback from EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to confirm target 1235 °C is achieved and stabilized prior to forging.
   Rationale: Ensuring billet temperature is stable at the specified target prevents substandard forging outcomes.

13. Production ramp and monitoring
   13.1. Ramp production to standard cadence as defined by the line leader and SOP-P1-L3-02 once the first parts meet dimensional and metallurgical checks.
   13.2. Monitor hydraulic pressures, cycle behavior, and control alarms for aberrant patterns.
   Records: Capture initial production run data and attach to the job traveler.

Records to keep
14. Maintain the following records in the document control folder for the shift:
   - Pre-start checklist signed by operator and supervisor.
   - Lubricant verification log indicating use of CFW-LUB-497 for EQ-P1-L3-HP02.
   - Temperature log from EQ-P1-L3-IH01 showing achieved setpoint 1235 °C for initial billets.
   - Dry run completion sign-off and any deviation reports.
   - First-piece inspection report and disposition.
   Example: Attach screenshots or printouts of PLC setpoint displays and the EQ-P1-L3-IH01 temperature trend for the first billet.

Deviations and nonconformance
15. If any step fails verification, stop the startup process, tag the failure per SB-1026, and notify maintenance and supervision. Record the failure in the shift log and reference ECN-2026-029 when configuration changes are suspected.

Operator and supervisor responsibilities
16. The primary operator performs steps 7 through 13 and records observations. The supervising technician verifies steps 2 and 3 preconditions and signs off on the pre-start checklist.

Sign-off
17. Completion sign-off required on the pre-start checklist by both the operator and the supervising technician. Retain signed checklist in the job folder and archive electronically per SOP-P1-L3-02.

Related documents
18. See ECN-2026-029 for engineering changes affecting start parameters, SB-1026 for safety bulletin actions, and SOP-P1-L3-02 for ongoing machining line operations and program control.
